description:
Most people get paid, pay their bills, and invest whatever is left over.

I do the exact opposite.

Every dollar of income flows into my brokerage account, gets invested into productive assets, and builds equity. I then use margin to pay regular living expenses while portfolio growth and dividend cash flow continue working inside the account.

In this video, I break down exactly how margin mechanics work and how I have been completely living out of my brokerage account since June 2024.

One year ago, my net portfolio value was approximately $129,000. Today, it is near $207,000—an increase of almost $80,000 while paying my mortgage, covering household expenses, and taking major family trips to Alaska and Japan directly from the brokerage account.

Over the last two years, my net portfolio value has increased by approximately $108,000 while I continued living out of the account.

This is not about recklessly borrowing money or simply chasing high dividends.

It is a system built around three layers:

Capital continuously entering the brokerage account
Long-term growth from stocks, ETFs, and closed-end funds
Dividend cash flow that helps cover margin interest and living expenses

My portfolio is currently projected to generate approximately $47,000 in forward dividend income over the next 12 months, or close to $4,000 per month.

At the same time, I have negotiated my margin interest rate down to 5.49%.

That creates a spread between the cash flow produced by my investments and the financing cost of accessing portfolio equity. But the real power is that money I would have immediately spent is instead converted into ownership of productive assets.

In this video, you’ll learn:

✅ How paycheck money flows into the brokerage account
✅ How deposits reduce margin and increase net equity
✅ How that equity can be redeployed into more assets
✅ How maintenance requirements affect available withdrawals
✅ The difference between gross portfolio value and net equity
✅ How dividends help offset margin interest and expenses
✅ Why growth, cash flow, and leverage must work together
✅ How I use E*TRADE’s margin calculator
✅ How I manage risk, volatility, and downside protection
✅ Why I treat my portfolio like a business

Over the last two years, while fully living out of the brokerage account, my portfolio produced an approximately 53% time-weighted return compared with roughly 35.5% for the S&P 500, 44% for the Nasdaq, 31% for the Dow, and 39% for the Russell 2000.

Borrowed money can make money—but only when the underlying assets, cash flow, portfolio structure, discipline, and risk controls are strong enough to support it.
